scenes.prompt: @Mike as a character model sheet on a plain cream ground, 16:9, three rows with small handwritten row labels. Top row, standing neutral at identical height: front view, left side view, three-quarter view, back view. Middle row, five head-and-shoulders portraits: happy, neutral, surprised, worried, angry. Bottom row, five full-body poses: waving, thinking with a hand at the chin, presenting with an open palm toward the viewer, explaining with both hands raised, shrugging. Consistent proportions in every cell, fully visible hands and feet. A light application of woodblock print and vox newspaper with rich anime colors. Negative: no text other than the row labels, no numbers, no charts, no logos.

A stick figure character as a character model sheet on a plain white ground, 16:9, three rows with small handwritten row labels. Top row, standing neutral at identical height: front view, left side view, three-quarter view, back view. Middle row, five head-only portraits: happy, neutral, surprised, worried, angry. Bottom row, five full-body poses: waving, thinking with a hand at the chin, presenting with an open palm toward the viewer, explaining with both hands raised, shrugging. Consistent proportions in every cell. He is a stick figure with a large round head, a big wide face and big expressive eyes behind black rectangular glasses, a small neatly trimmed goatee, warm brown skin, short sculpted loc twists on top of the head, a thin single-line black stick body with simple stick arms and legs and small round hands, and only a small flat deep-indigo suit block on the torso with a flat copper tie. Thick uniform black lines and solid flat colour fills so he reads at thumbnail size. Negative: no realistic anatomy, no detailed tailoring, no lapel pin, no shoes with pattern, no shading gradients, no text other than the row labels, no numbers, no charts, no logos.
scenes.note: v2 - a real stick figure (operator: big wide face and eyes, locs). No reference image: the detailed master pulled v1 into flat 2D Mike.

scenes.prompt: A stick figure character model sheet on a plain white ground, 16:9, three rows with small handwritten row labels, drawn with thick confident black ink brush lines of varying weight like a viral hand-drawn explainer cartoon. The character: a round head filled flat warm brown with tiny dot eyes behind bold black rectangular glasses, a single expressive mouth line, a tiny goatee, and a cluster of short locs drawn as a few bold black strokes on top; a thin black stick body with a small flat deep-indigo vest block and a copper tie, stick arms and legs, small round hands. He has attitude in every cell - narrowed eyes, a smirk, weight shifted, caught mid-motion with speed lines where he moves. Top row, standing at identical height with a cocky lean: front view, left side view, three-quarter view, back view. Middle row, five head-only expressions pushed to the extreme: happy as a smug grin, neutral as a dead-eyed stare, surprised as huge wide eyes and a tiny o mouth, worried as a sweat drop and wobbling mouth, angry as clenched teeth with anger veins on the forehead. Bottom row, five full-body poses drawn as action: waving big mid-stride, thinking with a hand at the chin and one eyebrow up, presenting with a sharp open palm thrust at the viewer, explaining with both hands flung up and motion lines, shrugging with a smirk and shoulders to the ears. Negative: no realistic anatomy, no shading gradients, no tailoring detail, no text other than the row labels, no numbers, no charts, no logos.
scenes.note: v3 - operator: 'the stick characters aren't cool, these guys look cool' (six reference frames: dot-eye heads, brush lines, extreme expressions, mid-action, prop-carried identity). Style traits described, no reference image.

roll_log.result: REJECTED - @Mike was literal prompt text with no chip; the model drew a different man. Flow moved to flow.google.com the same morning (driver patched: host match, media CDN).

LANDED - @Mike attached as a native chip (picker: type name, select, Add to prompt). Identity correct; layout loose (no back view, expressions across two rows, hero figure). Candidate for the contact sheet.

LANDED after three false downloads - the uploaded reference re-renders on the canvas as a new CDN image and Flow re-encodes it, so the detector took it as the output; fixed with an in-page perceptual hash exclusion, and references are now reused by filename instead of re-uploaded. Output 1376x768, on spec.

Three distinct sheets (one src collected twice; fourth still rendering at the 45s quiet cut-off). raw-4 matches the master: short tapered locs, pin, floral shoes, full 4/5/5 rows. raw and raw-3 drifted to long locs with @Mike bound and no re-description - the binding holds identity loosely under x4 variance.

Four real stick figures, no reference image. raw-2 recommended (widest eyes, rectangular glasses, most consistent); raw-4 alternate; raw-1 gave round glasses; raw-3 small eyes. A first run of this batch failed on a transient click timeout before submit.

The attitude landed: brush weight, speed lines, steam, smirk, extreme expressions. raw-3 recommended (labelled cells, strongest action row), raw-4 alternate. Miss: 'locs as a few bold strokes' produced three hairs - v4 changes only the hair line to a full crown of short locs.

Flow crashed mid-roll and recovered; the four images completed on the canvas and were pulled off it by URL rather than re-rolled. Full crown of locs held. raw-3 recommended (consistent in every cell, strongest action row), raw-4 alternate; raw-2 drops hair and glasses across the expression row.

Cream works. raw-1 came back on a deckle-edged cream page unprompted - the E22 ledger signature with the figure on it, which is the proof the drawing lane can carry both. raw-1 recommended (deckle, strongest attitude, 14/14 consistent); raw-2 alternate (soft pencil, no deckle); raw-3 drops skin fill on three heads; raw-4 painterly, locs long.
